text: Mr. Speaker, one year ago yesterday, my constituent James Henderson was killed with other aid workers from World Central Kitchen taking humanitarian aid into Gaza. Jim's family have told me Jim would want confirmation from our government that we're taking all conceivable steps to make sure that aid, power, and supplies are safely returned to Gaza. Could the PM confirm he's doing all he can to ensure this, and could the Prime Minister also confirm he will continue to push for a full investigation to be completed into the deaths of Jim and the other British WCK workers and for appropriate action to be taken?

Thank you, Mr. Speaker. I recently met around 20 independent local traders in Totnes who are furious that the last bank in town will close in January and that Link have refused to consider a banking hub. My businesses and constituents, 1100 of whom have signed a petition, deserve better. Now the Prime Minister has just told the member for Blyth and Ashington that a banking hub can be rolled out wherever a community needs one. So will he now back my campaign, ask his ministers to write to Link and instruct them to grant a banking hub to Totnes and to review the eligibility of rural towns for such hubs so that we can keep our vital high streets alive?

Before we come to Prime Minister's Questions, can I welcome in the gallery his Excellency, the honorable Stephen Francis Smith, the Australian High Commissioner to the UK. Stephen's term as High Commissioner comes to an end, we wish him all the best in retirement and thank you for what you've done in the UK. We now come to questions to the Prime Minister. Rachel Hopkins.

Mr. Speaker, the space sector is critical enabler in enabling our security, our ability to counter Russia and defend Europe. Can the Secretary of State explain how she is working with the new National Armaments Director and the MoD to develop a more cohesive approach to the space industry that delivers national security and economic growth?

Thank you, Mr. Speaker. In 2020, my constituents John and Karen Rowlands lost their son Andrew in a road collision. He was just 18 years old and a passenger. Like too many others, Mr. Speaker, the driver of the car should never have been on the road. He was underage, unlicensed and uninsured and bought the car on social media using cash. Can the Prime Minister tell me how bereaved families like the Rowlands can have a meaningful say on our road safety strategy and ensure the right checks are in place to prevent future tragedy?

Thank you, Mr. Speaker. The West Midlands car industry is world-famous and this government backs our automotive sector. We've got a US trade deal and when criminals shut down production at Jaguar Land Rover, we backed the supply chain. Brilliant companies like J.H. Lavender in my constituency. What a contrast with the member for Clacton, not here as usual, who said, 'I predict Jaguar will now go bust and they deserve to.' Would the Prime Minister agree with me that the workers of the West Midlands and the entire country need a Labour government and can't afford the economic vandalism of Reform UK?

Thank you, Speaker. People across Lichfield, Burntwood and the villages will be looking forward to a very Happy New Year, not least because of this government's commitment to the Midland Rail Hub project, which will revolutionize rail travel across the West Midlands and further afield. We are all really eager to see a better service between Lichfield and Birmingham as soon as possible though. So will the Prime Minister join my campaign for a more regular service on the Cross City Line, and can he confirm that rail commuters will benefit from frozen fares because of this Labour government?

Thank you, Mr. Speaker. Just days before Christmas, heartbroken Derbyshire families and staff have learned that the Reform-led council are closing eight care homes, including Rowthorne in Amber Valley. And that comes just days after learning that the council's cost-saving claims were entirely fabricated. Does the Prime Minister agree with me that when Reform talk about dross, what they're actually talking about is cutting vital public services and care homes, and will he join me in urging Derbyshire County Council to think again?

Thank you, Mr. Speaker. Labour's tax rises mean lower growth and higher unemployment, and the reason for the tax rises is government spending. The Prime Minister personally promised the country to limit spending increases to nine and a half billion pounds a year. So what mandate did he have in his first two budgets to increase annual spending 15 times faster by 146 billion pounds?

Mr. Speaker, over the past few weeks I've been contacted by a number of constituents who work in the health and care sector because they are concerned about the proposed changes to the rules surrounding indefinite leave to remain. These individuals came to this country to do a job we asked them to do, and then we decided to change the rules halfway through the process. Does the Prime Minister agree that if we are to be a proud rules-based nation, going back on our word to people who are contributing to our society and building lives here is not only just unfair, it's also profoundly un-British?

In September, a National Secular Society report highlighted alarming numbers of extremist religious organizations in the UK from various faith traditions, expressing hideous views about women, including promoting female genital mutilation and denying the existence of marital rape. Many of these are registered as charities and therefore eligible for various tax exemptions, as well as thousands or even millions of pounds in public money through gift aid. So will the Prime Minister, as part of the government's mission to halve violence against women and girls, support my campaign for a review of charity law and regulation so that we can make sure the UK taxpayer isn't funding extremism and hate?

Thank you, Mr. Speaker, and I'd like to thank the Prime Minister for his commitment to delivering the Hillsborough Law. But it has been proven that following the Manchester Arena bombings, MI5 spent six years misleading the public and concealing information. There was no risk to national security because it was a closed hearing. So will the Prime Minister deliver justice for those families and confirm that this government will bring forward an amendment that will make robust the duties and responsibilities of candor for all parts of the state, including individuals in the security services, so we can finally say never again?
